description:
## Outcome

        Jidoka has one provider-neutral lifecycle port and manager for `open`, `acquire`, `checkpoint`, `restore`, `fork`, `close`, and `cleanup`, with a deterministic conformance suite.

        ## Why now

        The special lifecycle operations must have exact semantics before session storage, CLI profiles, or LitterBox can depend on them.

        ## Current state

        No Jidoka environment port exists. `Operation.Source` can invoke tools but cannot own a durable environment lifecycle. Session stores already model lease-safe checkpoint and recovery, which the later story can reuse.

        ## Ownership and boundary

        This is a `jidoka` change. Adapters implement the port. The manager applies policy and evidence validation. Runtime handles stay transient in runtime context. The CLI never calls a provider or adapter directly.

        ## Detailed implementation

        1. Define exact callbacks: `open(resolved_profile, request, opts)`, `acquire(binding, opts)`, `checkpoint(handle, binding, opts)`, `restore(binding, checkpoint, opts)`, `fork(binding, checkpoint, opts)`, `close(handle, opts)`, and `cleanup(binding, opts)`.
2. Permit restore to rotate the portable binding identity and require the adapter to report it.
3. Require fork to use an immutable checkpoint. Return unsupported when the capability is absent.
4. Make close release one acquired handle while preserving durable state. Make cleanup idempotently destroy durable resources.
5. Run the host policy gate and pre-call validator before every operation. Validate returned evidence after every success.
6. Ensure all error paths close transient handles. Report cleanup failure separately from the primary error.
7. Add a fake adapter and reusable conformance tests for lifecycle order, evidence, idempotency, and failure behavior.

        ## Acceptance criteria

        - [ ] All seven operations have documented typed inputs and results.
- [ ] No runtime handle can enter a binding, checkpoint, snapshot, or session.
- [ ] Acquire is exclusive as defined by the adapter capability.
- [ ] Restore may replace binding identity and reports confirmed preservation facts.
- [ ] Fork rejects running mutable state and unsupported adapters.
- [ ] Close runs after success, error, and cancellation. Cleanup is idempotent.
- [ ] The conformance suite detects missing evidence and wrong call order.

        ## Test plan

        - Success: full open-acquire-checkpoint-close-restore-acquire-close-cleanup sequence and immutable fork.
- Invalid input: stale binding, mismatched checkpoint, cleaned binding, and nonportable adapter return.
- Runtime failure: fail each callback and verify close/cleanup ordering and error preservation.
- Boundary and security: policy deny and weak evidence must prevent the next capability call.
- Deterministic capability: fake adapter, resolver, policy, clock, and ID generator.
- JSONL and exit status: project lifecycle outcomes and errors as JSON-safe data for later CLI mapping.

        ## Documentation

        Add the lifecycle state machine and adapter author guide. Include callback tables, idempotency, cancellation, restore identity, and cleanup rules.

        ## Non-goals

        Do not integrate sessions yet. Do not implement Docker, LitterBox, SSH, or a local host shell. Do not store adapter handles.

        ## Dependencies

        Blocking issues:

        - `jido_cli-tqg.3.3` — Resolve trusted security profiles and fail closed

        Features unlocked by this story:

        - Durable session environment recovery
- Constrained shell and file tools
- Optional backend adapters

        ## Commit plan

        Create exactly one focused `jidoka` commit. Use a message such as `feat(jidoka): add the execution-environment lifecycle (jido_cli-tqg.3.4)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

        ## Verification commands

        ```sh
        cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jidoka
mix test test/jidoka/execution_environment/manager_test.exs test/jidoka/execution_environment/conformance_test.exs test/jidoka/runtime/effect_interpreter_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
        ```
title: Implement the execution-environment lifecycle manager
